tip: sekali = 'very', and it follows its word: deras sekali = very hard. In front, it means 'once' instead (sekali seminggu = once a week) – position decides.
-nya can do the job of 'the': kopinya sudah habis = the coffee is gone – the one you both know about. Indonesian has no separate word for 'the'.
ter- means it just happened, no doer in view: tertunda = got delayed. di- points at a doer: ditunda = was postponed by someone.
